Title: The University signs agreement with KESC to ensure steady electricity supply
NewsSummary: The Karachi Electric Supply Company (KESC) and Aga Khan University (AKU) signed an agreement here today for the establishment of a new 132-KV shared grid station.
NewsContent:
The Karachi Electric Supply Company (KESC) and Aga Khan University (AKU) signed an agreement here today for the establishment of a new 132-KV shared grid station. The agreement is a joint venture, where the cost of establishing the station would be shared equally between the two organisations. The new grid station will supply electricity to both the University and KESC's consumers in the area. KESC CEO, Tabish Gauhar and Aga Khan University President, Firoz Rasul signed the agreement.

The new grid station will ensure a steady electricity supply to AKU and Aga Khan University Hospital. It will also cater to the future needs of the University and University Hospital, where demand is expected to grow to 16 megawatts (MW) by the year 2022. "This grid station is being built to enable us to have access to secure power to allow us to continue to provide high quality health services to the patients who come to us for treatment from Karachi and from around the country," said President Rasul. Gauhar agreed and added, "This represents a significant investment for us and a symbol of support for institutions like AKU, where73 per cent patients come from low- and middle-income areas. Those unable to pay for treatment receive assistance through a variety of subsidies including the Hospital's Patient Welfare Programme that has disbursed Rs. 2 billion to more than 300,000 people since 1986. It is vital that we make a contribution to institutions that literally, keep Karachi alive and this is the first of a programme of such projects."

A task force comprising of professionals from KESC and AKU will oversee, manage and implement the planning, designing, construction and completion grid station. The station will be a state-of-art GIS grid to meet the total requirement of 11MW of electricity at the University and its teaching hospital, adding an additional 6MW to the existing 5MW. The commissioning of this grid, due in September 2011, will also relieve the overloaded grids of Civic Centre, Baloch Colony and Gulshan-e-Iqbal and will partially meet the requirement of future load growth in PECHS, Bahadurabad area, KDA Scheme-I and adjoining areas.
